mainTopic: Does רבי יהודה require a written document to give up a rabbinic money right, or is saying it enough? אביי answers by splitting common matters from uncommon ones, and the גמרא tests that answer with the case of the donkey drivers (חמרים).
overview: The גמרא finishes a contradiction in רבי יהודה. He seems to require writing to change a כתובה, but he lets a husband give up the produce (פירות) of his wife's property just by saying so. אביי answers that the רבנן reinforced common matters like the כתובה and not rare ones like פירות. The גמרא challenges this from the donkey drivers (חמרים), a common case where רבי יהודה adds no safeguard. אביי then splits definite rabbinic laws from doubtful ones, and רבא says the רבנן were simply lenient with דמאי. Next the גמרא explains רבי מאיר in the משנה: a stipulation to lower the כתובה is void, because he holds the כתובה is from the Torah. Still, the wife does not feel secure, so the relationship is like בעילת זנות. A ברייתא brings רבי יוסי, who allows lowering the כתובה. The גמרא asks how this fits with his worry about movable property losing value, and answers that here the woman knowingly gives up the money. The amud ends by starting a story about רמי בר חמא's sister, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Writing really means saying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its contradiction: in the case of the produce of a wife's property, 'writes' just means 'says'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we hold: what does 'writes' mean? It means 'says'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a challenge it started earlier. In the other case, where רבי יהודה says the husband 'writes' that he gives up the produce, the word really means he only has to say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יהודה seemed to require a written document to change the כתובה. In the produce case, though, spoken words are enough. So רבי יהודה seems to contradict himself about whether a rabbinic money right can be given up just by talking.

keyTerms.meaning: and we hold (an established rule)
writes
says

phrases.english: And we hold:
What does 'writes' mean? 'Says'!
phrases.notes: This is the word 'writes' from the case where a husband gives up the produce of his wife's property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contradiction raised before this section of text.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that the כתובה terms can only be changed in writing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the produce case רבי יהודה lets speech work, so why should the כתובה need writing?

steps.title: Common matters got extra strength, uncommon ones did not
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the כתובה is common, so the רבנן reinforced it, while the right to produce is uncommon, so they did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Everyone has a כתובה, but not everyone has produce. A common matter, the רבנן strengthened. An uncommon matter, the רבנן did not strengthen.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction. He says the two cases are different because one comes up all the time and the other doesn't.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every married woman has a כתובה, so the רבנן added a safeguard: changing it needs writing. Not every wife brings property into the marriage, so the right to its produce is rarer, and there speech is enough. רבי יהודה is consistent after all.

keyTerms.meaning: produce, the profits of the wife's property that the husband eats
a common matter
reinforcement, an extra safeguard added by the רבנן

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's rule: the רבנן add extra strength to common rabbinic matters, not to rare ones.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Everyone has a marriage contract,
but not everyone has produce.
phrases.notes: Not every wife brings property into the marriage, so not every husband has produce to eat.

phrases.english: A common matter —
the Sages made a reinforcement for it;
an uncommon matter —
the Sages did not make a reinforcement for it.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seemed inconsistent about speech versus writing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כתובה is common and was reinforced, so it needs writing. Produce is rare and was not reinforced, so speech is enough.

steps.title: Donkey drivers are common, yet no reinforcement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: donkey drivers are common, yet the רבנן did not reinforce the law for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But donkey drivers are common, and the רבנן did not make a reinforcement for them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's answer. It points to a common situation where, according to רבי יהודה, no extra safeguard was added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule is that common matters get strengthened, we would expect this for חמרים, who come into towns all the time. Yet רבי יהודה does not add strictness there. That breaks אביי's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: donkey drivers, traveling sellers of produce
but look, here is (a case)

phrases.english: But there are donkey drivers, who are common,
and the Sages did not make a reinforcement for it!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי חַמָּרִים דִּשְׁכִיחִי וְלָא עֲבַדוּ לַהּ רַבָּנַן חִיזּוּק
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that common matters receive a חיזוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here is a common case where רבי יהודה adds no safeguard, so 'common' cannot be the reason.

steps.title: The משנה about the donkey drivers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in דמאי: the תנא קמא does not believe a driver who praises his friend's produce, but רבי יהודה does believe him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: donkey drivers entered a city, and one said, 'Mine is new and my friend's is old; mine is not tithed and my friend's is tithed.' They are not believed. רבי יהודה says: they are believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for its challenge. It shows that רבי יהודה believes the drivers even though this situation is common.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion worries the drivers may be teaming up, taking turns praising each other's produce so each one sells. רבי יהודה does not add that worry, even though drivers are common. This seems to go against אביי's idea that common matters get extra strictness.

keyTerms.meaning: fixed, meaning the tithes have been taken
believed, trusted

steps.confusionAlert: Running down his own produce is not the problem. Nobody doubts a seller who says his own goods are worse. The question is whether we trust his praise of his friend's produce, since the two might be working together and taking turns.

phrases.english: As we learned:
Donkey drivers who entered a city,
and one of them said:
Mine is new, and my friend's is old.
phrases.notes: New produce is still moist and less good, so he is making his friend's sound better.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלִּי אֵינוֹ מְתוּקָּן, וְשֶׁל חֲבֵרִי מְתוּקָּן
phrases.english: Mine is not tithed, and my friend's is tithed —
they are not believed.
Rabbi Yehuda says: They are believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the challenge in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה does not add a safeguard for common situations
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה דמאי 4:7: רבי יהודה believes the donkey drivers

steps.title: אביי: The רבנן strengthen a definite law, not a doubtful one
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the כתובה is a definite דרבנן law, so it was strengthened. The donkey drivers' case is about a doubt, so it was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: For a definite rabbinic law, the רבנן made it stronger. For a doubtful rabbinic law, the רבנן did not make it stronger.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge from the donkey drivers by pointing to a new difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כתובה is a fixed rabbinic obligation that applies for sure. The donkey drivers' case is about דמאי, produce that only might not be tithed, so it is just a doubt. The רבנן added extra strength to definite laws, not to doubtful ones.

keyTerms.meaning: Definite; certain
Doubt; uncertain case
Of their words, meaning a rabbinic law

phrases.english: Abaye said:
For a definite rabbinic law, the Rabbis made a reinforcement.

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק דְּדִבְרֵיהֶם, לָא עֲבַדוּ רַבָּנַן חִיזּוּק.
phrases.english: For a doubtful rabbinic law, the Rabbis did not make a reinforcement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the donkey drivers raised in steps 3-4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: definite versus doubtful rabbinic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because donkey drivers are common, the רבנן should have strengthened that law too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Being common is not enough. The רבנן only strengthen laws that apply for sure, not doubtful ones.

steps.title: רבא: The רבנן were lenient with דמאי
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer: the רבנן were generally lenient about דמאי, so they did not strengthen the law in the donkey drivers' case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: With דמאי, the רבנן were lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers his own answer to the donkey-driver question, separate from אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא focuses on the topic of דמאי itself. The whole law of דמאי is already an extra stringency, since most people do tithe their produce. So the רבנן were lenient with it and did not add more strength.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce bought from someone who may not have tithed it
They were lenient

phrases.english: Rava said: With demai, they were lenient.
phrases.notes: He means the רבנן were easygoing about דמאי, because most people tithe anyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the same challenge that אביי answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the challenge to the special topic of דמאי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The donkey drivers' case shows the רבנן do not strengthen common laws.
steps.terutzMaskana: That case is special because דמאי as a whole was treated leniently.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers: אביי says definite laws get strengthened but doubtful ones do not. רבא says דמאי is a lenient area to begin with.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: Lowering the כתובה even by agreement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי מאיר from the משנה and explains that it applies even when there is a stipulation. The stipulation is void, but since the woman was told she gets less, she does not feel secure, so the relationship is like בעילת זנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: Anyone who lowers the amount, etc. 'Anyone who lowers' means even through a stipulation. So he holds the stipulation is void and she does have the full amount. But since he told her 'You only have a מנה,' she does not feel secure, and his relations with her become like בעילת זנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, רבי מאיר's ruling, and explains how it works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'anyone' teaches that even a stipulation the wife agreed to is included. Legally the stipulation is void and she can still collect the full כתובה. But she was told she only gets a מנה, so she does not rely on it. That lack of security is what makes the relationship like בעילת זנות.

keyTerms.meaning: One who lowers (the כתובה amount)
A stipulation; a condition agreed on
His stipulation is void
She does not feel secure; she does not rely on it
Relations like those outside of marriage

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר does not say she loses money. Legally she still has the full כתובה. The problem is that she does not feel secure, because she was told she gets less.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַפּוֹחֵת וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: Anyone who lowers, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: lowering below two hundred for a virgin or a מנה for a widow.

phrases.english: 'Anyone who lowers' means even by a stipulation.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר תְּנָאוֹ בָּטֵל, וְאִית לַהּ.
phrases.english: Apparently he holds his stipulation is void, and she has the full amount.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵיוָן דְּאָמַר לַהּ ״לֵית לִיךְ אֶלָּא מָנֶה״ —
phrases.english: But since he told her, 'You have only a maneh,'
she does not feel secure,
and his relations with her become licentious relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַפּוֹחֵת וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a stipulation to lower the כתובה is void, yet the marriage is still like בעילת זנות because the wife does not feel secure.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's rule: stipulations against the Torah are void
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: רבי מאיר himself said only a stipulation against a Torah law is void. That implies a stipulation against a rabbinic law, like the כתובה, should stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we heard that רבי מאיר said: Anyone who makes a stipulation against what is written in the Torah, his stipulation is void. That implies that for a rabbinic law, his stipulation stands!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction between step 7 and another known ruling of רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר voids only stipulations that go against the Torah. The כתובה is usually seen as rabbinic, so a stipulation to lower it should work. So why did step 7 call it void?

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes a stipulation
What is written in the Torah
His stipulation stands

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: But we have heard Rabbi Meir say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמַּתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה —
phrases.english: Anyone who makes a stipulation against what is written in the Torah,
his stipulation is void.
This implies that with a rabbinic law, his stipulation stands!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation in step 7 that the stipulation is void.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי מאיר holds a stipulation lowering the כתובה is void
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר's own rule only voids stipulations against Torah law. The כתובה is rabbinic, so the stipulation should stand.

steps.title: רבי מאיר holds the כתובה is from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר holds the כתובה is a Torah law. So lowering it is a stipulation against the Torah, which is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds that the כתובה is from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction from step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כתובה is a Torah obligation, then lowering it goes against the Torah. That fits רבי מאיר's rule, so the stipulation is void, just as step 7 said.

keyTerms.meaning: The כתובה is a Torah obligation

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds that the ketubah is from the Torah.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing which category רבי מאיר places the כתובה in
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כתובה is rabbinic, so a stipulation against it should stand.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי מאיר the כתובה is from the Torah, so the stipulation is void.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר voids a stipulation to lower the כתובה because he holds the כתובה is from the Torah.

steps.title: ברייתא: רבי מאיר, רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה on lowering the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings three opinions. רבי מאיר says lowering the כתובה makes it like בעילת זנות. רבי יוסי says it is allowed. רבי יהודה says he may write the full amount, and she writes a receipt saying she already got part of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי מאיר says: Anyone who lowers the כתובה below two hundred for a virgin or below a מנה for a widow, this is בעילת זנות. רבי יוסי says: It is allowed. רבי יהודה says: If he wants, he writes a document of two hundred for a virgin, and she writes him 'I received a מנה from you.' For a widow he writes a מנה, and she writes him 'I received fifty זוז from you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that shows the full disagreement about lowering the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר forbids lowering the amount. רבי יוסי allows it. רבי יהודה allows a way around it: the document shows the full amount, but she writes a receipt saying she already received part, so she can really collect only the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: He is allowed
A written document
I received (wording of a receipt)
A coin, the same as a דינר

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir says:
Anyone who lowers it below two hundred for a virgin
or below a maneh for a widow,
phrases.notes: A מנה is one hundred זוז.

phrases.english: this is licentious relations.
Rabbi Yosei says: He is allowed.
Rabbi Yehuda says: If he wants,
he writes a document of two hundred for a virgin,
and she writes him: 'I received a maneh from you.'
phrases.notes: So in practice she can collect only the other hundred.

phrases.english: And for a widow, he writes a maneh,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִיא כּוֹתֶבֶת לוֹ: ״הִתְקַבַּלְתִּי מִמְּךָ חֲמִשִּׁים זוּז״.
phrases.english: and she writes him: 'I received fifty zuz from you.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַפּוֹחֵת לִבְתוּלָה מִמָּאתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that expands the dispute about רבי מאיר's ruling from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר says lowering the כתובה is not allowed. רבי יוסי allows it. רבי יהודה allows a full document plus a receipt for part of it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא sets up the three opinions that the גמרא will go on to analyze.

steps.title: Does רבי יוסי really allow lowering the כתובה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יוסי really allows lowering the כתובה. It sets up a contradiction from a ברייתא where רבי יוסי worries that a כתובה from movable property might lose value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוסי really hold that a husband may lower the כתובה? Here is a contradiction. A ברייתא teaches: a woman's כתובה may not be paid from movable property, for the good of society. רבי יוסי said: what good does that rule do? Movable items have no fixed value, and they can lose value!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא doubts רבי יוסי's ruling from step 10 and quotes a ברייתא that seems to show him worried about a woman getting less than her כתובה. This step sets up the challenge; the next steps work out exactly what the ברייתא means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, רבי יוסי said a husband is רשאי, allowed, to lower the כתובה. Here he seems concerned that movable property might lose value and leave the woman short. That concern seems to clash with letting the husband openly give her less.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction: one source seems to clash with another
Movable property, such as tools, clothing or furniture, as opposed to land
For the good of society; a rule the חכמים made to keep things running fairly
Fixed in value
They lose value

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yosei hold that he is permitted?
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא just quoted, where רבי יוסי said a husband may lower the כתובה.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
One may not make a woman's marriage contract from movable property,
because of the betterment of the world.
Rabbi Yosei said:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה תִּיקּוּן הָעוֹלָם יֵשׁ בְּזוֹ?
phrases.english: And what betterment of the world is there in this?
But they are not fixed in value, and they lose value!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוסי's view in step 10 that lowering the כתובה is allowed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's ruling that a husband may lower the כתובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Elsewhere רבי יוסי seems worried that a woman might receive less than her כתובה, so it seems odd that he would let the husband deliberately give her less.

steps.title: The first opinion seems to say the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices a problem inside the ברייתא. The first opinion already says a כתובה may not come from movables, so what is רבי יוסי arguing about?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the first תנא also says 'one may not make' it from movables! What is the argument?
steps.whatsHappening: Before using the ברייתא, the גמרא has to understand it. Both opinions seem to forbid using movables, so the גמרא asks where they actually disagree. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's words sound like a protest, but the first תנא already forbids movables. So the two opinions must disagree about some specific case. The next step explains which case that is.

keyTerms.meaning: The first תנא; the opinion stated first in the ברייתא, without a name
Also

phrases.english: The first tanna also says "one may not make" it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the wording of the ברייתא brought in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both opinions forbid movables, רבי יוסי's statement adds nothing and there is no argument.

steps.title: They argue about movables backed by a guarantee
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the ברייתא. The first תנא allows movables if the husband guarantees them. רבי יוסי forbids movables even with a guarantee, because their value can drop.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this must be what the first תנא means. The rule against movables applies when the husband did not accept a guarantee. If he did accept a guarantee, it may be done. רבי יוסי comes to say: even with a guarantee, why may it be done? Movables have no fixed value, and they can lose value!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where the two opinions really disagree: about movables backed by the husband's guarantee. רבי יוסי is the stricter one, because he still worries the value will drop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the contradiction is sharper. רבי יוסי is so worried about the woman losing value that he forbids movables even with a guarantee. That seems hard to match with his permission in step 10 to lower her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? A phrase that limits a rule to a certain case
A guarantee; taking responsibility so that she is covered
Rather, isn't it so that... (introduces the reading the גמרא is pushed into)

phrases.english: Rather, isn't this what he is saying:
In what case are these words said?
When he did not accept a guarantee upon himself,
but if he accepted a guarantee upon himself, one may make it.
And Rabbi Yosei comes to say:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קִיבֵּל עָלָיו אַחְרָיוּת אַמַּאי עוֹשִׂין?
phrases.english: Even when he accepted a guarantee, why may one make it?
But they are not fixed in value, and they lose value!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו הָכִי קָאָמַר: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by explaining exactly where the two opinions disagree.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא: the argument is about movables backed by a guarantee
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both opinions seem to forbid movables in every case, with no real argument.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first תנא allows movables if the husband guarantees them. רבי יוסי forbids them even then, because their value can drop.

steps.title: If a possible loss worries him, surely a certain loss does
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the challenge with a קל וחומר. If רבי יוסי worries about movables that might lose value, he should surely object to a כתובה that is definitely lowered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now think about it. There, the movables might lose value, and still רבי יוסי is worried. Here she definitely loses part of her כתובה, so shouldn't he object all the more?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the ברייתא is clear, the גמרא states the full challenge against רבי יוסי as a קל וחומר: from a possible loss to a certain loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With movables the loss is only a maybe, yet רבי יוסי forbids it even with a guarantee. Lowering the כתובה is a sure loss. So it seems רבי יוסי should never allow it, which goes against his view in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: Now; here it means 'now think about it' and opens a קל וחומר
Perhaps, maybe
All the more so

phrases.english: Now,
just as there, where perhaps they will lose value,
Rabbi Yosei is concerned,
here, where he definitely gives her less,
is it not all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the explained ברייתא from step 13 to complete the challenge against step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's permission to lower the כתובה (step 10)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: if a possible loss worries him, a certain loss should worry him even more.

steps.title: She agreed to the loss here, but not there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. With movables, the woman does not know she may lose, so she never agreed to it. When the כתובה is lowered, she knows and agrees to give up part of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, she does not know she might lose, so she never gave anything up. Here, she knows exactly what she is losing, and she agrees to give it up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing the two cases are different. What matters is whether the woman knowingly gives up the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With movables, the drop in value is a surprise, so she never agreed to it, and רבי יוסי protects her. When the כתובה is lowered, the amount is stated openly and she accepts it. A woman may give up money that belongs to her. So רבי יוסי's two rulings do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? A phrase that rejects a comparison
She gives up, she forgives (the money owed to her)
That she should give it up

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי, the problem is a loss the woman never agreed to. If she knowingly accepts a lower כתובה, she has given up her right, so it is allowed. If the loss is a surprise, as with movables that drop in value, he protects her.

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, she does not know, so that she could give it up,
here, she knows, and she gives it up.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי הַשְׁתָּא?! הָתָם לָא יָדְעָה דְּתַחֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 14 by showing the two cases differ.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the cases differ: knowingly giving up money versus a loss she did not expect
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A certain loss should be worse than a possible loss, so רבי יוסי should forbid lowering the כתובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A loss the woman knowingly accepts is allowed. Only a hidden loss she never agreed to is a problem.

steps.title: A new story: רמי בר חמא's sister
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story: the sister of רמי בר חמא was married to רב אויא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sister of רמי בר חמא was married to רב אויא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new story connected to the laws of the כתובה. This line only sets the scene; the story continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא moves from discussing opinions to a real case. The line only introduces the people involved, and the halachic question comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: His sister
Married (to)

phrases.english: The sister of Rami bar Ḥama
was married to Rav Avya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story after the רבי יוסי discussion is resolved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet; this line introduces the people in the story.
